svg.title: Choose Mirroring, Dataflow Gen2, or Pipeline Ingestion
svg.desc: A decision flowchart helping architects choose between Database Mirroring, Dataflow Gen2, and Data Factory Pipelines based on replication, visual transformation, and high-throughput orchestration needs.
svg.text: Ingestion Strategy: Mirroring vs Dataflow Gen2 vs Pipelines
Architectural Decision Tree · Continuous CDC Replicas · Visual Power Query Shaping · Orchestrated Batch Movement

g.title: What must ingestion do? — Classify the requirement as continuous replication, low-code shaping, or controlled movement.
g.text: Root Decision: What is the Primary Ingestion & Transformation Requirement?
Classify by latency target, transformation location, developer persona, and operational maintenance overhead:
A. Need near-real-time OLTP sync with 0 ETL ➔ Mirroring
B. Need visual Power Query transformations ➔ Dataflow Gen2
C. Need high-throughput batch movement & control flow ➔ Pipeline

g.title: Managed Mirroring — Choose Mirroring for a supported source needing a continuously maintained Delta replica.
g.text: LANE A: MANAGED MIRRORING
Near-Real-Time Delta Replica
• Continuous log-based CDC replication in seconds
• 0 pipeline authoring, scheduling, or maintenance
Ideal Scenarios & Strengths:
✓ Operational reporting over Azure SQL, Cosmos, Snowflake
✓ Power BI Direct Lake reports update automatically
✓ 0 ingestion CU billing (completely free movement compute)
✓ Protects transactional OLTP from analytical load
Automatic Delta compaction & V-Order optimization
Boundaries & Constraints:
❌ Supported source databases only (Azure SQL, Cosmos, Snowflake)
❌ Primary keys mandatory on all replicated tables
❌ In-flight transformations NOT supported (pure 1:1 replica)
❌ Complex DDL alterations can pause replication stream
Trap: Mutable replica overwrites history (Deletes propagate)
Requires separate append-only pipeline for permanent audit log.
Architectural Verdict:
Default to Mirroring when you have a supported operational
database and need sub-minute analytical Direct Lake queries
without writing or managing ETL data pipelines.

g.title: Dataflow Gen2 shaping — Choose Dataflow Gen2 when visual Power Query transformation is the primary need.
g.text: LANE B: DATAFLOW GEN2 (POWER QUERY)
Low-Code Visual Transformation
• 300+ out-of-the-box Power Query M transformations
• Lakehouse staging compute accelerates query folding
Ideal Scenarios & Strengths:
✓ Business analysts & citizen developers shaping feeds
✓ Cleansing, pivoting, typing, and standardizing data
✓ Ingesting diverse flat files, spreadsheets, and Web APIs
✓ Direct output destinations: Lakehouse, Warehouse, SQL
Visual step-by-step lineage & column profiling
Boundaries & Constraints:
❌ Non-foldable queries fall back to single container evaluation
❌ High CU consumption on multi-terabyte raw file extractions
❌ Scheduled batch runs (cannot match near-real-time CDC)
❌ Complex recursive procedural loops are hard to maintain
Trap: Forcing multi-terabyte bulk migration into Dataflow
Use Pipeline Copy for raw bulk movement; transform in Lakehouse.
Architectural Verdict:
Use Dataflow Gen2 when business logic requires visual Power
Query cleansing on small-to-medium datasets before loading
into Lakehouse tables.

g.title: Pipeline Copy — Choose Pipeline Copy for scheduled or dependency-aware movement with explicit controls.
g.text: LANE C: PIPELINE COPY & ORCHESTRATION
High-Throughput Scalable Movement
• 100+ connectors across cloud, on-premises & SaaS
• Intelligent Throughput Optimization (ITO: 4–256 units)
Ideal Scenarios & Strengths:
✓ Terabyte-to-petabyte scalable migrations into OneLake
✓ Complex control flow (ForEach, Until, If/Else, Webhooks)
✓ Orchestrating multi-step pipelines (Copy ➔ Notebook ➔ PBI)
✓ Built-in retry policies, parameters, and failure handling
Standalone Copy Jobs offer simplified bulk/incremental CDC
Boundaries & Constraints:
❌ No complex row-by-row data transformation in flight
❌ Requires explicit watermark management for incremental batch
❌ Non-idempotent copy retries can cause duplicate rows
❌ Scheduled intervals incur polling latency vs streaming
Trap: Authoring pipelines when Mirroring already supports DB
Check Mirroring source catalog first to eliminate custom ETL.
Architectural Verdict:
Default to Pipeline Copy for all raw high-volume ELT ingestion
from external clouds, filesystems, and databases not supported
by native Fabric Database Mirroring.

g.title: Validate the operating fit — Compare source support, acceptable lag, transformation ownership, recovery, and capacity impact.
g.text: Validate Operating Fit & Guardrails
Five-point architectural validation checklist
1. Source Support: Check native connector vs mirror catalog
2. Freshness SLA: Sub-minute (Mirror) vs Batch (Pipeline)
3. Transformation: Visual M vs PySpark vs Pushdown SQL
4. Idempotency: Ensure replay/retries never duplicate data
5. Capacity Sizing: Account for 24h background smoothing
Validation Gate Rule:
Document the Ingestion Decision Record (ADR) detailing why
a primitive was selected, its failure modes, and recovery runbook
before deploying to production workspaces.

g.title: Replica is not immutable history — A current-state mirror can lose past states unless history is captured separately.
g.text: CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL TRAP
Replica is NOT Immutable History
Mirroring maintains current state, not permanent audit logs
• Hard deletes at source propagate immediately to Delta replica.
• Overwritten records are purged once Vacuum threshold lapses.
• Delta Time Travel is temporary retention, NOT a 7-year audit store.
Architectural Remedy:
Separate current-state replication from append-only ledger capture.
Use Mirroring for real-time operational BI, and pair with a Pipeline
or Eventstream writing immutable append-only Bronze tables for SCD2.

g.title: Compose behind clear contracts — Combine Mirroring, Dataflow, and Pipelines only when each owns a distinct boundary.
g.text: Compose Behind Clear Data Contracts
Production multi-tool hybrid architecture pattern
Combine services with strictly decoupled boundaries:
• Mirroring: Provides live operational current-state replica
• Pipeline: Ingests raw batch archives & coordinates dependencies
• Dataflow Gen2: Cleanses small reference lookup datasets
Golden Architecture Rule:
Never allow multiple tools to write to the same Delta target table.
Enforce strict Medallion boundaries: each tool owns its isolated
Bronze/Landing dataset before unified Gold refinement in Lakehouse.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Fabric Ingestion Architecture Specs.
